drug_class: Microsomal triglyceride transfer protein (MTP) inhibitor / lipid-lowering agent
purpose: Lomitapide is used to lower very high levels of bad cholesterol (LDL cholesterol) and fats in the blood in adults with a rare inherited condition called homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH). This condition makes it extremely hard for the body to remove cholesterol on its own. It is used along with a low-fat diet and other cholesterol-lowering treatments.
how_it_works: Your liver normally uses a special protein to package fats and ship them into your bloodstream. Lomitapide blocks that protein, called MTP, so your liver makes and releases much less bad cholesterol into your blood. Think of it like stopping a factory from shipping out products — less gets sent out, so levels in your blood go down.
common_side_effects: Stomach and digestive problems are very common, including diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, and feeling full quickly. You may also notice oily or fatty stools. Fatigue and headache can also occur. These side effects are often less bothersome if you eat a very low-fat diet.
warnings: Lomitapide can cause serious liver problems, including liver damage. Your doctor will regularly check your liver with blood tests. Because of this risk, it is only available through a special restricted program called a REMS program — not every pharmacy carries it. Do NOT take it if you are pregnant, as it can seriously harm an unborn baby. Avoid grapefruit juice and certain medications (like some antibiotics and antifungals) that can raise lomitapide levels dangerously. Always tell your doctor about all medications and supplements you take.
typical_dosing: You usually start with a low dose of 5 mg taken by mouth once a day at bedtime, at least 2 hours after your evening meal. Your doctor will slowly increase your dose over several months, up to a maximum of 60 mg per day, based on how well you tolerate it and how your liver is doing. Always take it on an empty stomach at night and follow a very low-fat diet (less than 20% of calories from fat).
